brief.headline: Blackstone targets $3bn for real estate secondaries fund
bullets: Real Estate: Blackstone is seeking to raise at least $3bn for a new real estate secondaries fund, targeting discounted stakes in existing property vehicles as liquidity pressures continue across the sector, according to Bloomberg.

M&A & Buyouts: Advent International is seeking to sell Singapore-based education provider The Learning Lab for between $400m and $500m, marking its second attempt to exit the business since 2021, according to a report by Bloomberg.

Infrastructure & Energy: Blackstone-backed Rowan Digital Infrastructure has secured approximately $1.5bn in additional financing to support the development of its US data centre portfolio, as investment in artificial intelligence infrastructure continues to drive demand for capacity, according to a report by Bloomberg.
Family Offices & Wealth: The value of sports media rights is soaring: The global sports media market grew 41% from 2020 through 2025 and has continued climbing to an expected $67 billion in 2026.

Regulation & Policy: The Securities and Exchange Commission today proposed rule amendments to make its executive and director compensation disclosure requirements more principles-based and materiality-driven, providing investors with clearer, more concise.
brief.marketRead: Bottom line: calm volatility and open credit markets are a supportive backdrop for dealmaking, fundraising and exits. The S&P 500 stands at 7,592.4 (down 0.4% on the prior reading) and the VIX is 18.7, a normal-volatility reading. The effective fed funds rate is 3.88%, the 10-year Treasury yield is 4.98% (up 10 bps on the prior reading) and the 10Y–2Y yield curve is +0.24 pts (nearly flat). High-yield credit spreads are 3.20%, near long-run norms (down 10 bps on the prior reading).
